title: Every failed message is either retried later or parked in the DLQ
caption: Transient errors get another try after a growing delay. A message that keeps failing is moved aside so it stops blocking or burning the consumers.

steps.text: The consumer receives a message and runs the handler.
Success: ack, and the broker deletes the message.
Failure: has it already used up its attempts?
Not yet: put it back with a delay of base × 2^attempt plus jitter (1 s, 2 s, 4 s…). It comes back to 'Run handler' later.
Out of attempts: it's a poison message. Park it in the dead-letter queue, alert, and replay it by hand once the bug is fixed.

scenarios.name: Transient error
scenarios.summary: A timeout on the first try, success on the second: the retry path exists for errors that go away on their own.

steps.text: The handler calls a downstream service, which times out.
First failure, so attempts are left.
Back on the queue with a short delay plus jitter. Meanwhile other messages overtake it, so order isn't kept.
Next time round the downstream has recovered: the handler succeeds and the message is acked.

scenarios.name: Alternative: classify first
scenarios.summary: Ask whether the error can ever succeed before spending retries on it: a validation error goes straight to the DLQ.

steps.text: Look at the error first. Timeouts, 503s and lock conflicts may succeed later.
A malformed payload or a failed validation will fail the same way every time: park it at once, without burning 3 attempts and their delays.
Only retriable errors enter the attempt counter and the backoff loop.

scenarios.name: Risk: retry forever
scenarios.summary: Without an attempt cap, a poison message loops for ever, burning consumers and (in ordered queues) blocking everything behind it.

steps.text: A message with a bad payload arrives. The handler throws.
There's no cap, so the answer to 'attempts left?' is always yes.
It comes back, fails again, and again: forever. Each try costs a worker, and in a FIFO queue or a log partition nothing behind it moves.
Mitigation: cap attempts, back off exponentially, send the rest to the DLQ and alert on its depth.
